lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The Leafs keep flirting with momentum, then hand it back - a 2-2-1 club sitting fifth in the Atlantic, one point out of fourth, but now carrying a one-game skid. The latest blow came Thursday, a 4-3 loss to Vegas, another narrow defeat that leaves Toronto searching for the extra save and the cleaner finish. Kirill Marchenko, meanwhile, is making his presence felt with the kind of direct, forceful play this lineup has needed, while John Tavares will miss tonight's game after the birth of his son. Nick Paul moves into the second-line center role, a substantial promotion against Colorado's speed and depth. Five points through five games is neither crisis nor comfort. The margin is already visible. Tonight at 7 p.m. ET in Colorado, watch whether Toronto can defend the middle of the ice and turn a competitive start into a winning road statement.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The season is over, and Toronto's offseason has already found its first test: stop treating Vladimir Guerrero Jr.'s talent as a substitute for direction. Joey Votto's blunt advice - "Watch your dad" - puts the spotlight on Guerrero's approach, a timely reminder that the club's best hitter needs clarity, not another round of vague expectations. At 79-83 and fifth in the AL East, the Blue Jays need more than a cosmetic repair. They need impact. The encouraging news is arriving from below: JoJo Parker's first professional season has strengthened the organization's belief that he can remain at shortstop, while the Arizona Fall League offers another look at the next wave, including prospects with loud raw tools. That matters because Toronto cannot buy its way out of every roster flaw. Watch whether the club adds a proven outfielder and gives Parker a genuine path upward - those decisions will define the winter.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The Raptors' preseason has already delivered a warning shot: Toronto was flattened 129-105 by Miami on Oct. 3, an exhibition defeat that counts for nothing but exposes plenty. The club has no regular-season record or standings position yet, and that is precisely why tonight's Vancouver test matters as a rehearsal, not a verdict. Kawhi Leonard, the blockbuster arrival, completed his first full live practice Friday but will sit against the Clippers as Toronto manages his ramp-up. That leaves Scottie Barnes, RJ Barrett and Immanuel Quickley to carry the visible load while rookie Allen Graves studies how the veterans operate and makes his case for a place in the rotation. The roster math is tightening; lineup clarity is not. Watch Saturday at 6:30 p.m. ET for the young players' response, then Leonard's possible return before Toronto opens the regular season against Chicago on Oct. 21.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The slogans and brotherhood have worn thin; Washington needs a win, not another locker-room sermon. The 30-13 loss to Indianapolis last Sunday dropped the Commanders to 1-3, fourth in the NFC East, with a one-game skid and two games to make up. The offense now gets a jolt - Jayden Daniels is cleared to return from his dislocated left elbow, though he is not yet at full strength. That makes Lucas Patrick's permanent move to center more than a lineup footnote; protection must hold while Daniels finds his legs again. Washington's task is complicated by a Giants attack arriving intact: Malik Nabers, Cam Skattebo, Isaiah Likely and Andrew Thomas are all expected to play. No excuses remain. Sunday's 1 p.m. meeting with New York is a referendum on whether this season can be rescued or merely prolonged.

article.title: Leafs Visit Avalanche Without Tavares
paragraphs: The Leafs visit the Avalanche tonight at 7:00 p.m. ET on Sportsnet, with Anthony Stolarz projected in goal against Mackenzie Blackwood. Toronto is 2-2-1 and John Tavares is out for personal reasons after the birth of his son; Nick Paul is expected to take his spot between William Nylander and Easton Cowan. Oliver Ekman-Larsson is day-to-day.

The Raptors play the Clippers at 6:30 p.m. ET in a preseason game, with Kawhi Leonard among those unavailable. Toronto's regular season opens against the Bulls on Wednesday, October 21. The Jays are looking ahead to their farm system, with JoJo Parker among the prospects drawing attention.

The Commanders host the Giants Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET on Fox. Washington is 1-3 and Malik Nabers has no injury designation for New York. For now, the next confirmed appointment is at Northwest Stadium.
